questions.help:
Priorities, level crossings and tunnels  
 
5 Narrow Sections
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
When there is a narrow stretch of road and there are no signs or signals to determine priority, the vehicle that has entered into the restricted area first will normal continue through having priority over vehicles coming from the opposite direction.
If there is however doubt or conflict, the vehicle that has the greatest difficulty manoeuvring will have preference.
(Página 209 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Priorities, level crossings and tunnels      
     
5 Narrow Sections  
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
5.2.1 Order of preference in the absence of road signs
The following explains the order of preference in the absence of road signs, signals or authorised persons, and applies to priority when different types of vehicles approach a narrow road section and it is necessary for one of the vehicles to reverse back to allow the other vehicle to pass. Under these circumstance priority is given as follows:
1.Special vehicles and those travelling under special regulations that exceed the established masses and dimensions as per the regulated rules of vehicles (MAM).
2. Set of vehicles-except those within point 4 below.
3. Vehicles pulled by animals.
4. Cars that tow a trailer of up to 750 kilograms MAM and camping vehicles.
5.Public transport vehicles-designed to transport passengers.
6. Lorries, tractive units and good vans and goods vehicles.
7. Car and vehicles derived from cars.
8. Special vehicles that do not exceed the mass or dimension established within the regulating laws; heavy quadricycles and light quadricycles.
9. Three wheeled vehicles, motorcycles with sidecar and three wheeled mopeds.
10. Motorcycles, two wheeled mopeds and bicycles.
(Página 209 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Priorities, level crossings and tunnels      
     
5 Narrow Sections  
5.2 Narrowing section without signed priority
5.2.1 Order of preference in the absence of road signs
If the vehicles are the same type or are not listed above, preference will be given to the vehicle that has the furthest distance to reverse. If there are two vehicles that have an equal distance to reverse, then priority will be given to the one that has the greater width, length or MAM.
(Página 209 del manual 'Learning to drive')

A continuous longitudinal marking means that no driver, whether operating a vehicle or leading an animal, must:
Cross it.
Drive on it.

12.1 The reaction distance
The reaction distance is the distance travelled by the vehicle from the time of seeing a hazard until he reacts to it.
It is dependant on the speed and the driver’s reaction time, which in turn depends, on many other factors, such as, the driver’s reflexes, their psycho-physical state (level of alertness, whether or not the driver is under the influence of alcohol etc.) Even the environment can affect the time it takes for a driver to react to any given circumstance (the passenger compartment temperature, noise, etc.)

questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.2 The braking distance
The braking distance is the distance the vehicle travels from the point at which the driver first applies the brakes, until the vehicle come to a complete stop.
This distance can vary depending on:
The speed of the vehicle at the point the brakes are applied.
The mass of the vehicle and its load.
The technical condition of the vehicle (brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, etc.)
The environmental conditions and the condition of the road surface (snow, rain, state of the surface, etc.)
The driver (psychophysical status –mental and physical state, experience, etc.)
An increase in speed causes the braking distance to increase, but this is at a greater rate than the speed increase.
Thus, when the velocity is doubled the braking distance is four times higher.
(Página 179 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Additionally, you cannot exceed the maximum authorised mass per axle or the maximum authorised mass of the set or combination.

When it is not possible to continue forwards, or change direction (turn to the left or right) or complete a ‘U’ turn. For example the road ahead is blocked, or closed or there is a narrow stretch of roadway etc.).

Maneouvres        
 
8 Reversing
As a general rule, reversing backwards is prohibited. However, as an exception it is permissible (but only when travelling a minimum distance backwards – in reverse gear), in the following two cases:
When reversing forms part of one of the following manoeuvre, parking, stopping or joining the traffic flow. In this instance the distance travelled in reverse gear must not be further than 15 metres and you must not invade a junction.
(Página 195 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
5 Generic speed          
       
5.2 Maximum speeds within a populated area
As a general rule, the maximum speeds within populated areas, except for those vehicles with a lower maximum speed limit, are:
On urban roads with a single platform for carriageway and pavement: 20 km/h.
In urban lanes with one carriageway per direction of travel: 30 km/h. (*)  
- Personal mobility vehicle: 25  km/h.
In urban lanes with two or more carriageways per direction of travel and in through-roads: 50 km/h.
- Vehicles transporting hazardous goods: 40 km/h.
- All other vehicles: 50 km/h.  
- Personal mobility vehicle: 25  km/h.
(*) The lanes reserved for certain users or for exclusive use by public transport are not considered for these purposes.
The generic speed limit on motorways and dual carriageways that pass through a populated area will be 80 km/h.
(Página 174 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Journeys and defensive and efficient driving  
 
8 Efficient driving
Economic and efficient driving means employing a system that saves fuel, reduces pollution and eliminates any unnecessary expense whilst not compromising safety.
(Página 275 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Journeys and defensive and efficient driving  
   
9 Efficient driving techniques  
9.3 Travelling speed
Therefore, it is advisable to moderate the speed and keep it as consistent as possible, adapting it to the road and traffic conditions. The continuous variation of speed will increase fuel consumption, and in heavy traffic, driver fatigue will occur.
It is advisable to drive evenly, this means avoid hard braking, harsh acceleration and unnecessary gear changes, maintain a consistent speed for as long as possible.
Use the techniques of preventive driving: drive always with anticipation and awareness, maintain an adequate safety distance and keep the field of vision as broad as possible, so as to be able see 2 or 3 vehicles in front.
Unnecessary stopping and starting and speed variations caused by the lack of foresight and anticipation increase consumption.
(Página 277 del manual 'Learning to drive')
